title: stream session resilience and termination policy for OpenAI-compat layer
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers reported two classes of production instability when using long lived streaming sessions through the OpenAI compatibility adapter: abrupt disconnections leaving incomplete tool/function calls, and client-driven cancel semantics that produced ambiguous server state. This PR adds an explicit session negotiation + termination contract, explicit client cancel tokens, and robust server-side idle/active timeouts to make streams deterministic and resumable where possible. Changeset summary: 1) Protocol: introduce optional Stream-Session header with a server-issued session_id and resume_token. Clients may present resume_token within 30s to pick up an in-flight stream. 2) Cancel semantics: adds a client-cancel event ("CANCEL_TOKEN" frame) that reliably marks in-progress function/tool calls as cancelled; server responds with an acknowledgement frame before stopping the stream. 3) EOF and structured output: add an explicit EOF control frame ("STREAM_EOF") and a small framing extension for structured output chunks so tooling functions can be reassembled deterministically after reconnects. 4) Timeouts: server now enforces two timeout tiers: active_token_timeout (max time waiting for client ACK during a tool call) and session_idle_timeout (max idle time before session eviction). Defaults were chosen to be conservative (active 45s, idle 120s) with config overrides per deployment tier. 5) OpenAI-compat adapter: preserve existing OpenAI-compatible chunked data shape but add a top-level meta chunk that contains session_id/resume_token when available so existing SDKs remain compatible while opt-in resume semantics are supported. 6) SDK updates: exposed session resume API in JS/TS and Python SDKs plus a cancel() convenience. 7) Tests & observability: added unit and integration tests covering reconnect resume in the happy path and simulated partial tool execution aborts; added per-session metrics (session_start, session_resume, session_eof, session_eviction) and tracing baggage to link function calls across reconnects. Checklist: - [x] Protocol design doc (linked internal spec) - [x] Implementation in service runtime - [x] Adapter mapping for OpenAI-compat - [x] SDK surface for resume/cancel - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Add metrics and alerts Rollout: staged behind feature flag streaming_resume in main and enabled for canary customers first. Backwards compatibility: adapter returns resume metadata only when the client and server advertise support through headers; non-upgraded clients continue to receive standard chunked responses with no behavioral change. Related linear: ENG-1124 (streaming stability spike), ENG-1190 (tool-call idempotency).

reviews: Diego: Please clarify how call_id maps to tool invocation retries; requested deterministic call_id generation for idempotent retries. Author: added call_id field in the framing and deterministic generation based on request nonce and sequence number.
Maya: Add observability hooks to distinguish EOF vs eviction. Author: added session_eof/session_eviction metrics and trace tags; updated observability doc.
Samir: Concerned about default timeouts being too low for slow external tools. Author: exposed config overrides per deployment and added a canary config with longer defaults for tool-heavy customers.

release_notes: Improved streaming session resilience: server-issued session_id and resume tokens enable reconnect-and-resume for short disconnects; explicit client cancel frame and server ack to make tool/function call cancellation deterministic; new STREAM_EOF control frame for reliable structured output termination; server-side active and idle timeouts configurable per deployment; SDK updates (JS/TS/Python) expose resume and cancel helpers; enabled behind feature flag streaming_resume. No breaking changes for older clients.
